summary: The article accurately details SEBI's new regulations for Gold and Silver ETFs, including effective dates, changes to price band calculations, dynamic price bands, pre-open call auctions, and the shift to domestic valuation for physical gold holdings.

claims.claim: SEBI has introduced new regulations, effective from September 1, 2026, to fix these discrepancies and improve price accuracy.
claims.note: SEBI's new framework for ETFs, including dynamic price bands and revised base price calculations, will come into effect from September 1, 2026.

claims.claim: Additionally, from April 1, 2026, Gold and Silver ETFs must value physical gold using domestic spot prices instead of international benchmarks, enhancing transparency.
claims.note: SEBI has mandated mutual funds to use domestic stock exchange spot prices for valuing their physical gold and silver holdings from April 1, 2026.

claims.claim: One of the most significant changes is the shift in how the base price for an ETF's daily trading band is determined. Instead of the T-2 NAV, exchanges will now use the previous day's (T-1) closing market price. Specifically, this base price will be derived from the Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) of the last 30 minutes of the previous trading session.
claims.note: SEBI has changed the methodology for determining ETF base prices. Instead of using the T-2 NAV, exchanges will use the previous day's closing price, calculated as the Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) during the last 30 minutes of trading.

claims.claim: Under the new rules, Gold and Silver ETFs will have an initial dynamic price band of ±6%. If the price hits this threshold, the band can be expanded in stages of 3% after a cooling-off period, depending on market conditions and international commodity price movements.
claims.note: Commodity ETFs tracking gold and silver will have an initial price band of ±6%, which can be expanded in stages of 3% after a cooling-off period.

claims.claim: To address this, SEBI is introducing a pre-open call auction mechanism for Gold and Silver ETFs. This is similar to the mechanism used for regular equity shares at market open.
claims.note: SEBI has mandated a pre-open call auction session for gold and silver ETFs to improve price discovery, similar to the mechanism used for regular equity shares.

claims.claim: Previously, funds relied on international benchmarks like the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA) AM fixing prices, which then required multiple adjustments for currency conversion, customs duty, and other local factors.
claims.note: Until March 31, 2026, the NAV of Gold and Silver ETFs was calculated using the AM fixing price published by the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA), which required adjustments for currency conversion, customs duty, transportation costs, applicable taxes and levies, and a notional premium or discount.

article_title: Gold ETF Pricing: How SEBI is Ensuring Fairer Value for Investors
